meeting_header:
Date: 2026-02-19
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 55 min
Attendees: Alex Marino (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Vellum Eng Manager), Priyanka Rao (Vellum SRE), Marcus Nguyen (Vellum Head of AI), Elena Park (Vellum Product)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on telemetry tuning and finalizing canary ramp plan. Agreed scope for a short synthetic load window, defined SLO/alert thresholds to gate the canary, and ownership for runbook handoff. Customer raised a minor security question about KMS usage in private deployment; AE to follow up with SOC2 docs.

Runbook ownership and on-call rehearshal, spelled rehearsal intentionally
VPC peering and allowlist for test traffic
transcript: [00:00] Alex Marino: Hey team, thanks for keeping this on the calendar. We planned 55 minutes; main goals are telemetry tune, canary thresholds, and runbook ownership handshake.

[00:27] Jordan Lee: Thanks Alex. Quick note, Priyanka had to jump in late, so if we repeat anything that's fine. We did the baseline test yesterday, results were a bit noisy on p95, wanted to go over that.

[00:45] Priyanka Rao: yeah sorry, I was on another thread. The 30min spike around 10:40 was likely from an integration test hitting cache misses, we need to confirm whether Redwood's prefix cache warmed. Marcus, do you want to add?

[01:15] Marcus Nguyen: Sure, it looked like the KV cache wasn't primed for the longer seq patterns. Some prompts had long system tokens, so per-token latency popped. But overall throughput was steady. We're mainly concerned with tail latency for user-facing flows.

[01:48] Priya Desai: From Redwood side, we instrumented KV hit-rate and prefetch warm-up; dashboard link is in the deck, but I'll share the direct template after the call. The runtime has a fast-path for quantized weights, but warm-up matters for early canary buckets.
[02:22] Elena Park: Can you explain the warm-up behavior in more concrete terms? Like, how many requests to get to stable p95?

[02:40] Priya Desai: ballpark, with our current config and the Vellum prompt shapes, 50 to 200 requests for the prefix to be in memory. It varies by model and seq length. For the pilot, we recommend a 30 minute burn-in with synthetic traffic to pre-warm caches before traffic ramp to real users.
[03:12] Jordan Lee: Ok, so we should run a 30 minute warm-up with synthetic traffic then wait 10 minutes before starting canary ramp?

[03:28] Alex Marino: That's one pattern. Another is to route 5% of traffic to the canary for 15 minutes with heat-up enabled; Redwood's auto-warm policy will keep KV primed. We should decide which is operationally simpler for your on-call team.
[03:55] Priyanka Rao: Our SREs prefer an explicit warm-up window to avoid false positives in alerts. We had an alert storm previously when a canary warmed and triggered thresholds before stabilizing.
[04:20] Priya Desai: Totally fair. We'll propose thresholds that ignore initial warm-up — like suppressing alerts for 20 minutes post-launch for canary buckets. I'll add that to the runbook.

[05:01] Marcus Nguyen: Moving to metrics - we want p95 < 350ms for chat completions, error rate < 0.2% and token cost within 10% of baseline. Can Redwood compute cost delta per token in the dashboard?

[05:25] Alex Marino: Yes, the console shows token-level cost and a delta over baseline per model/route. We'll share a sample dashboard and CSV export. That's one of the docs I'm sending after this call.
[05:59] Jordan Lee: Great. What about A/B vs Canary? We were thinking of an A/B experiment for quality guard-rails, while using canary for capacity changes.

[06:19] Priya Desai: They're complementary. For model quality comparisons, A/B routing with 50/50 for a controlled subset is useful. For rollout safety we use canary ramps with traffic gates and SLO gates. We can run A/B inside the canary group if you want simultaneous quality measurement.
[06:48] Elena Park: That would be nice — surface quality metrics (BLEU-ish or custom eval) alongside latency so product can decide. Do you support custom eval metrics in the console?
[07:04] Priya Desai: Yes, Redwood Optimize can push custom eval sets and surface regression alerts based on your prompt set. For the POC, we can add a small prompt set for the A/B.
[07:26] Jordan Lee: Security point — Marcus raised KMS isolation concerns. If we run private deployment, who manages the keys?

[07:42] Alex Marino: In Private mode, customers can integrate their KMS/HSM — Redwood supports customer-managed keys and you maintain control. For Dedicated (hosted dedicated), we offer tenant-isolated keys but we still manage the HSM side. I'll attach explicit docs.
[08:05] Marcus Nguyen: Ok, please include the KMS flow and audit log retention. We need proof for our internal auditors.
[08:20] Alex Marino: Noted — action item, I'll send SOC2 + KMS flow and retention specifics.
[08:34] Priyanka Rao: Back to canary thresholds: what's the suggested ramp schedule? We need numbers we can give on-call.

[08:45] Priya Desai: Recommended is: 0% -> 5% for 15 min -> 20% for 30 min -> 50% for 30 min -> 100% if all gates pass. Each step gated by p95, error rate, and cost delta. If any gate exceeds threshold, automatic rollback to previous stable.
[09:16] Jordan Lee: Those times feel short — can we extend the 20% window to 60 minutes? Our user sessions can be long and the sample size matters.
[09:30] Priya Desai: Sure. We can make 20% a 60 min hold. That will increase exposure but gives better stability signals. We'll update the runbook example.
[09:50] Elena Park: On alerts during canary, we want a separate severity routing so on-call only gets paged for critical degradation. Can Redwood integrate to PagerDuty?
[10:03] Alex Marino: Yes, we have native PagerDuty and Slack integrations. You can map thresholds to PD escalation policies. We'll show an example PD playbook in the runbook template.
[10:28] Marcus Nguyen: Question about autoscale burst capacity: if we see a sudden delta in tokens we want an agreed burst cap so cost doesn't spike. How should we configure?

[10:45] Priya Desai: Configure a burst window and a cap in the deployment settings. Redwood also supports cost-based routing to a lower-cost model variant when unit cost exceeds threshold. That keeps availability without runaway cost.

[11:12] Jordan Lee: Hmm, I like the idea of fallback variants. For the pilot, we want to avoid any service-level change that degrades quality for users. Maybe fallback to a busy-signal style short message rather than a lower-quality model.
[11:30] Priya Desai: That's possible — policy can return a structured error or a short degraded response. We'll document options and recommended patterns.
[11:53] Alex Marino: Quick sync on ownership: who on Vellum will be primary on-call during the rehearsals and go-window?
[12:05] Jordan Lee: Priyanka will be primary SRE; Marcus will be AI lead for quality issues; Elena is product owner for go/no-go. I'll make that formal in the runbook.
[12:25] Elena Park: I'll add escalation contacts and calendar windows to the doc after this meeting.
[12:40] Priyanka Rao: One operational request: can Redwood emit a short-lived runbook URL that we can hand to the on-call during the canary? A single page with steps, rollback, and PD links.
[12:55] Priya Desai: Yes — we can produce a one-page runbook link and an abbreviated checklist. I'll send both and a PDF copy.
[13:12] Jordan Lee: Regarding monitoring telemetry - what exact metrics should we include in the required sightlines?

[13:25] Priya Desai: Required: p50/p95/p99 latency, request/sec, tokens/sec, error rate, KV cache hit rate, model-variant distribution, token-cost-per-request. Optional: quality eval score and user-visible success rate.
[13:52] Marcus Nguyen: Can Redwood stream those metrics to our existing Prometheus? We prefer centralized alerting.
[14:05] Priya Desai: Yes — metrics can be exported to Prometheus or via Datadog. For Prometheus, we'll provide a scrape endpoint in the private deployment or an agent for hosted.
[14:28] Jordan Lee: Great. Let's talk about the rehearsal schedule — we propose two rehearsals: one dry run of the runbook, one load-rehearsal with synthetic traffic. Can we do them next week?
[14:45] Alex Marino: Redwood is available Tuesday and Thursday morning PT. Which works for you?
[14:55] Jordan Lee: Thursday morning works better for our SREs. Let's tentatively pick 2026-02-26 09:00 PT for the load-rehearsal and 2026-02-24 11:00 PT for the dry run.
[15:18] Elena Park: We also need a post-rehearsal retro — 30 minutes to capture lessons, ops notes, and tweak thresholds.
[15:31] Priya Desai: We'll add a retro agenda to the calendar invites.
[15:45] Marcus Nguyen: One last technical note: we observed minor tokenization differences between the two model variants; can Redwood ensure identical tokenizer config?

[15:59] Priya Desai: We can pin tokenizer and vocabulary at model versioning; Redwood's model catalog includes tokenizer metadata. I'll confirm the exact tokenizer hash used in your test model and share it.
[16:20] Jordan Lee: Docs and artifacts — what will be shared after this call?
[16:31] Alex Marino: I'll share SOC2 + KMS doc, Priya will share dashboard template, canary thresholds in a spreadsheet, and a one-page runbook. Links will be in the follow-up email.
[16:48] Elena Park: For the acceptance criteria for go-decision, let's be explicit: 48hr synthetic run with p95 within threshold, zero critical errors, and quality delta within 5%.
[17:05] Priya Desai: That aligns with Redwood's recommended acceptance criteria. We'll add a checklist item to the runbook and mark responsible owners.
[17:26] Jordan Lee: Anything we missed?
[17:32] Alex Marino: We covered main items. I'll recap next steps now then open for any final clarifications.

[17:45] Alex Marino: Recap — Redwood to send SOC2/KMS doc, dashboard template, canary thresholds, and one-page runbook by Monday 2026-02-22. Vellum to provision test networking and run the 48hr synthetic window by 2026-02-26. Schedule rehearsals for 2026-02-24 (dry run) and 2026-02-26 (load rehearsal).
[18:12] Jordan Lee: Sounds good. Priyanka, Marcus, any last comments?
[18:20] Priyanka Rao: Nothing else from SRE, just please make the runbook concise and call out warm-up suppression to prevent alert noise.
[18:32] Marcus Nguyen: No further comments. Thanks everyone.
[18:40] Alex Marino: Thanks team, we'll follow up with the artifacts and invite updates. Meeting adjourned.
[18:48] [call ends]
